newsitem.title: USA: Oil, wheat gain on weather, precious metals drop.
newsitem.headline: Oil, wheat gain on weather, precious metals drop.

text.p: Oil prices rose Wednesday on forecasts for cold weather in the Northeast as traders shrugged off increases in oil product inventories last week.
Gold prices, which have fallen to the lowest levels in more than three years, dropped along with other precious metals.
The Knight Ridder Commodity Research Bureau index of 17 futures contracts fell 0.21 point to 242.17.

Oil prices were led higher by heating oil, which fell initially on reports of a higher-than-expected rise in stocks, but then turned higher on forecasts for cold weather in the Northeast, the world's largest heating oil market.

The Energy Information Agency reported Wednesday that stockpiles of disillates, which include heating oil and diesel fuel, rose a sharp 3.1 million barrels last week, in line with the American Petroleum Institute's report on Tuesday.

Heating oil prices, however, later turned higher after a number of forecasters changed their earlier predictions of normal weather for the northeastern United States and instead looked for cold weather extending into next week.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February heating oil futures rose 0.94 cent to 73.43 cents a gallon. February crude oil gained 39 cents to $26.62 a barrel.
"It is really just a very resilient market. There was not only some short-covering but some new buying," said Thomas Blakeslee, a trader at Cargill Investor Services in New York.
February unleaded gasoline ended 0.09 cent a gallon higher at 72.19 cents.

Natural gas, which had ended official trading higher on the cold weather forecasts, tumbled in after hours trading when the American Gas Association reported an unexpectedly small weekly drawdown in U.S. gas stocks.
February natural gas futures gained 17.9 cents per million British thermal units to $3.513, but fell in after-hours trading to $3.46.
Precious metals futures ended sharply lower with gold and platinum futures hitting fresh life-of-contract lows.

"It's a continuation of the erosion in the precious metals complex that's been going on for some time, driven by funds, rather than central bank activity," said Merrill Lynch commodity research director William O'Neill.

At the New York Mercantile Exchange's Comex division, February gold ended down $2.90 an ounce at $356.80 after setting a new contract low at $355.30. Gold is at the lowest level since September, 1993, when prices hit a low of $343.
March silver closed down 5 cents at $4.660.

Spot gold prices have fallen about 3.5 percent in the first four trading days of 1997, and the slump Wednesday was partly inspired by a report from industry consultants Gold Fields Mineral Services, which said a rise in official sector sales was the main cause of gold prices weakness in late 1996, traders said.
Official sector sales -- meaning government-held metal -- totalled an estimated 123 metric tons in the second half of 1996 and an estimated 208 tons total for the year, Gold Fields said.

Meanwhile, investment demand for physical bullion and gold coins remained at its lowest level since the 1970s, with the U.S. stock market setting new record highs and drawing interest away from precious metals.
NYMEX April platinum closed down $3.20 an ounce at $363.90 after seeing a new contract low at $362.20. Earlier, platinum hit a three-year low at $358.50 in London in the morning.
At the Chicago Board of Trade, March wheat posted a gain for the third straight day on worries about potential "winter kill" in the Southern Plains this weekend.
March wheat ended 2-1/2 cents a bushel higher at $3.95.

A frigid cold front will move across the hard red winter wheat belt beginning Thursday and temperatures by the weekend could drop to 10 to 15 degrees (Fahrenheit) below zero in Kansas, said forecaster Jon Davis with broker Smith Barney.
Lack of snow in the Plains, combined with a sharp freeze, could kill young wheat plants now dormant for the winter in the Plains states, where half of the U.S. wheat crop is grown.
